transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I feel like I’ve shut down and keep reacting badly ever since my work fell apart. I just can’t seem to handle anything that reminds me of trying to get back into business.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'shut down' and how you react badly when reminded of getting back into business, is it more like feeling extremely sad, anxious, or detached from things you used to enjoy?

It’s more of a mix of dread, anxiety, and shame—whenever I see paperwork or get a voicemail, my mind goes blank and I end up hiding in my garage or going to the river. I've also felt really detached and have pulled back from things I used to enjoy, like my club and volunteering, because the pressure is just too much. It's like I'm just avoiding everything.

Is your dread, anxiety, and avoidance primarily triggered by reminders of your work or business, or have you experienced these feelings in response to other stressful events or situations in your life as well?

It’s really just triggered by the business falling apart and anything that reminds me of trying to get back to work. Before all of this happened, I was able to handle things and juggle my responsibilities just fine. I honestly think that if I could just get the business side sorted out, this whole spiral would ease up.
Can you tell me more about what specifically happened with your business that led to it falling apart, and was there a particular event or moment that you feel triggered this reaction in you?

About six months ago, my handyman business fell apart because I procrastinated on licensing and insurance paperwork, which cost me a major contracting opportunity and caused a dispute with a long-time client. Around the same time, my chronic back pain got worse, pushing me completely out of the workforce. Losing that big contract and realizing I had to shut down was the specific trigger, and within a few weeks of that happening, I started freezing up and shutting down.

You mentioned that your business fell apart about six months ago and you started experiencing these symptoms shortly after; have you had any periods in the past six months where you felt significantly better or were able to function more normally for a while, or has it been a consistent struggle since then?

It has been a consistent struggle for the past five months since everything collapsed. I haven't really had any periods of feeling better or functioning normally, because the constant stress of the financial pressure and unfinished paperwork triggers that same shutdown response every single time it comes up.

Can you describe if there are any specific thoughts, memories, or emotions related to your business failure that you repeatedly experience or try to avoid, and how these thoughts affect your daily life and interactions with others?

Whenever my wife mentions paperwork or a customer leaves a voicemail, I get hit with this wave of dread and shame that makes my mind go blank, so I avoid those feelings by hiding in the garage or going to the river. This avoidance has really strained my relationship with my wife, who is stressed about our finances, and it has caused me to completely pull back from my community volunteer work and club activities.

Can you tell me if you experience any flashbacks, nightmares, or severe physical reactions when reminded of your business failure, such as the licensing and insurance issues or the dispute with your client?
No, I don't experience any nightmares or flashbacks about what happened. It's more of a sudden wave of dread and shame that makes my mind go blank, rather than reliving the events in that way.

Can you tell me more about what specifically happens when you 'hide in the garage' or 'go to the river' - are you trying to escape the feelings of dread and shame, or is there something else that you're trying to achieve or avoid in those moments?

Yes, going to the garage or the river is definitely my way of trying to escape those intense feelings of dread and shame. Whenever I'm faced with business reminders, my mind goes completely blank and the pressure feels too heavy, so I retreat to those places to avoid dealing with the situation entirely. I always end up feeling incredibly guilty, though, because I know my avoidance is only making things worse.
You mentioned feeling guilty about avoiding your responsibilities, can you tell me more about how this guilt affects you and if it's present even when you're not directly reminded of your business?

The guilt is mostly about not contributing financially to my family, especially with rising living costs and my daughter's college tuition. While the sharp dread and blanking out only happen when I'm directly confronted with business stuff, that background guilt is a constant, heavy weight. It lingers even when I'm trying to escape at the river or in my workshop, constantly reminding me that I'm not pulling my weight.

Can you describe if there are any specific aspects of your daily life, aside from business-related tasks, where you feel you're able to function normally or experience pleasure, or if the avoidance and guilt have affected all areas of your life equally?

The avoidance and guilt have definitely bled into other areas of my life, causing me to pull back from my club activities and community volunteering. I feel like I'm not pulling my weight at home, and even when I try to escape to my workshop, I can't focus enough to finish anything, leaving my projects half-organized.

You've mentioned pulling back from activities you used to enjoy, like your club and volunteering, but are there any activities or hobbies that you still find some pleasure in or look forward to, even if it's just a little?

I still spend time alone on the river or in my workshop, but those are really the only things I do these days. They feel more like a way to escape my stress and avoid responsibilities rather than something I actually enjoy, and I usually end up leaving my workshop projects half-finished.

Can you describe how you would feel and react if you were suddenly given the opportunity to restart your business with all the necessary support and resources, would your dread, anxiety, and avoidance diminish or persist?

I really think that if I had that kind of support to get the business side sorted out, the dread and avoidance would definitely diminish. Since this whole shutdown is tied directly to my business falling apart, getting it back on track with the right resources would likely cause this entire spiral to ease up.

If you were able to resolve the business issues and get back on your feet financially, do you think you would still experience the same level of dread, anxiety, and detachment from activities you used to enjoy?

No, I don't think I would. This entire spiral is directly tied to the business falling apart, whereas before this happened, I was able to handle my responsibilities just fine. I genuinely feel that if we got the business side and our finances sorted out, the dread, anxiety, and detachment would pretty much ease up.

You've mentioned that resolving the business issues would likely ease up your symptoms, but can you think of any other stressful life events or situations, aside from your business, that could potentially trigger similar feelings of dread, anxiety, and avoidance in you?

Well, my worsening chronic back pain is a major stressor because it physically limits my ability to do heavy handyman work. On top of that, the heavy financial pressure of rising living costs and my daughter's community college tuition constantly weighs on me, making me feel incredibly guilty for not contributing.

You've mentioned that your business failure and chronic back pain are significant stressors for you, but can you tell me if you think you would experience similar dread, anxiety, and avoidance if you were faced with a different kind of significant stressor, such as a serious illness in a family member or a major conflict with a loved one?

I'm really not sure how I would react to something like a family illness or a major conflict, since I haven't had to deal with those kinds of situations recently. In the past, I was usually able to juggle life's challenges just fine, so this overwhelming dread and shutdown feels very specifically tied to my business falling apart and my physical limitations.

If you were to experience another significant life stressor unrelated to your business, such as a serious family issue, do you think your reaction would be similar to what you've experienced since your business fell apart, or do you think you would be able to cope differently?

I'm not really sure how I would handle a completely different stressor like a family issue since I haven't thought about it much. Before my business fell apart, though, I generally felt like I could juggle life's challenges okay.

You've mentioned that your reaction seems very specifically tied to your business falling apart and physical limitations, but can you think of any past experiences where you faced a significant stressor and did not shut down or experience this level of dread and anxiety?
I can't really recall any past major stressors like this to compare it to. Before all of this happened, I was always able to juggle normal life and work pressures just fine without shutting down.

If you were to resolve your business issues and your chronic back pain was managed, do you think you would still have difficulty coping with new, unrelated stressful events, or do you believe your ability to handle stress would return to how it was before your business fell apart?

Yes, I definitely believe my ability to handle stress would go back to how it was before. Before the business fell apart, I was able to juggle everything just fine, and I feel this shutdown is directly tied to these specific issues. If those were resolved, I really think this whole spiral would ease up.

You believe that resolving your business issues and managing your chronic back pain would significantly improve your ability to cope with stress, but can you think of any other factors or stressors that might still trigger feelings of dread, anxiety, or avoidance in you, even if your business and back pain issues were fully addressed?

No, I really don't think there would be any other triggers. Before the business collapsed and my back pain got worse, I was able to handle life's demands and juggle everything just fine. I truly believe that if those specific issues were sorted out, this whole dread and avoidance would completely go away.

You've consistently tied your symptoms to your business failure and back pain, but can you imagine any scenario where you might experience similar dread, anxiety, and avoidance in response to a completely unrelated stressor, or do you believe your reaction is uniquely tied to these specific issues?

I absolutely believe this reaction is uniquely tied to these specific work and financial issues. Before my business fell apart, I was able to juggle life's challenges and responsibilities just fine without ever freezing up like this. I keep thinking that if I could just get the business and work situation sorted out, this entire spiral of dread and avoidance would ease up.

You've mentioned that your symptoms are triggered by reminders of your business failure, but can you think of any other situations or reminders that might trigger a similar response in you, or is it exclusively related to your business?

It is exclusively related to the business falling apart and the pressure to get it back on track. Things like paperwork, customer voicemails, or discussions about restarting are what trigger me to freeze up and hide away. Before this work crisis, I handled everything fine, and I really believe that if I could just get the business sorted out, this whole spiral would ease up.
